title: Score du cuir chevelu du nourrisson (Nourrisson Scalp score)
short_title: Score du cuir chevelu du nourrisson (Nourrisson Scalp score)
formula:
The Infant Scalp Score is calculated by the addition of the selected points:

| Variable | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patient age (month) | >12 | 0 |
| 6-11 | 1 | |
| 3-5 | 2 | |
| 0-2 | 3 | |
| Hematoma size | None | 0 |
| Small (barely palpable) | 1 | |
| Medium (easily palpable) | 2 | |
| Large (boggy consistency) | 3 | |
| Hematoma Location | Frontal | 0 |
| Occipital | 1 | |
| Temporal/Parietal | 2 | |

how_to_use.why:
- Les nourrissons peuvent présenter une lésion cérébrale traumatique (TBI) même s’ils ne montrent que des symptômes limités.
- Ce score aide à déterminer le risque de lésion intracrânienne en fonction de l’âge du patient et des caractéristiques de l’hématome.
- Si le patient est jugé à faible risque, une imagerie de la tête peut ne pas être nécessaire.
how_to_use.when:
- À utiliser chez les nourrissons asymptomatiques au moment de l’évaluation mais présentant un risque élevé de fracture du crâne.
- Aide le clinicien à déterminer si une imagerie crânienne (TDM cérébrale) est nécessaire dans le bilan d’une lésion intracrânienne.
how_to_use.pearls:
- This tool was studied in asymptomatic patients and should be applied only to patients in that population.
- This tool should not be used in patients who have any of the following:

 - Loss of consciousness.
 - Lethargy or irritability.
 - Seizures.
 - 3 or more episodes of emesis.
 - Mental status changes.
 - Bulging fontanel.
 - Signs of neurologic injury.
 - Abnormal vital signs.
- It should also not be used in infants who present with suspected nonaccidental trauma.
- Measurement of skull hematoma characteristics is somewhat subjective; the PECARN data set used in a large validation study (see Evidence) categorized hematomas as <1 cm or barely palpable, 1–3 cm, and >3 cm and/or boggy.
- Primary outcomes differed in various validation studies, with one using skull fracture and another using the outcome of clinically important traumatic brain injury (ciTBI).

next_steps.advice: - L'évaluation pour traumatisme non accidentel n'est pas nécessaire chez tous les nourrissons ayant subi un traumatisme crânien, mais la possibilité doit toujours être envisagée, en particulier chez les nourrissons qui ne marchent pas encore ou ne se déplacent
next_steps.critical_actions:
- Cet outil ne doit pas être utilisé chez les nourrissons pour lesquels un traumatisme non accidentel est suspecté ; suivre les protocoles institutionnels pour les décisions d’imagerie crânienne dans ces cas, et envisager fortement une consultation avec un pédiatre spécialisé en maltraitance infantile.
- Même lorsque le motif principal de consultation est un traumatisme crânien, rechercher d’autres lésions.
next_steps.management:
- For patients with a score <4, head imaging may not be necessary.
- For patients with a score≥4, head imaging (usually with a CT) should be considered.
- Some[studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32673432/)have recommended a cutoff of≥5 for ciTBI.
- As with all risk assessment scores, clinical judgment is essential.

evidence:
The[derivation study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11334100/)evaluated 422 infants; 11% were diagnosed with skull fracture and 3% with intracranial injury. The tool demonstrated a sensitivity of 0.98 and specificity of 0.49 for skull fracture. All 13 cases of intracranial injury were detected. Skull fracture and intracranial injury correlated with hematoma size and location, and weakly with younger age.

A[prospective validation study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20805783/)in 2010 found that a score ≥4 had a sensitivity of 0.90 and specificity of 0.78 for detecting skull fractures. A score ≥3 had a sensitivity of 0.93 and specificity of 0.42 for intracranial injury.

A[second validation study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32673432/)in 2021 of 1289 infants (12 months of age and younger) found a sensitivity of 1.0 and specificity of 0.49 for a cutoff of ≥4 points for detecting clinically important traumatic brain injury, defined as death from TBI, neurosurgical intervention, intubation≥24 hours for TBI, or hospitalization ≥2 nights for TBI. AUC was 0.916 for clinically important TBI and 0.807 for any TBI, defined as any intracranial bleeding, pneumocephalus, cerebral edema, skull fracture with depression of at least the thickness of the skull, or diastasis (abnormal cranial suture separation) of the skull. It is important to note that although retrospective, this study used the robust multi-center PECARN dataset, which may strengthen its validity.

More recent validation studies have shown similar performance. A[single-center retrospective study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36056932/)performed at an academic medical center in Turkey (Guneysu et al., 2023; n = 380) found a cutoff of 4 had a sensitivity of 100% and a specificity of 70.9%. Even with a cutoff of 5 (representing a higher threshold to image), no patients with clinically important TBI were missed. A[prospective single-center study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12271540/)from Iran showed similar performance at a higher cutoff value. With a cutoff of 6, the AUROC was 0.876, and a cutoff of 7 had an AUROC of 0.890. A higher cutoff may better stratify high- versus low-risk patients, but further research is needed. No society guidelines have endorsed a specific threshold. Injury risk assessment should be individualized, and shared decision-making with families is appropriate in most circumstances.
more_info:
Interpretation:

| Infant Scalp Score | Risk of TBI |
| --- | --- |
| <4 | Low |
| ≥4 | High |
